reason: WP 5.5, measured with node x perf labs/box --scene room on the development platform (Chromium 141 on SwiftShader at 960 x 540, 20 cores at a load average of 35 to 42 from up to 6 lanes): 120 steps, then 60 frames drawn. The counts were the same in three runs and are the budgets, so with the 15% tolerance a room that draws 5 more calls, adds 3 textures or builds one pipeline after the warm-up fails, and its WP records the new counts with its reason. The means of the last 60 steps and frames were 0.013 to 0.14 ms a step (0.003 to 0.105 of them physics, no anim) and 2.1 to 3.1 ms of CPU a frame; their budgets leave about 7x and 4x over the loaded means, so only a real regression fails. Re-recorded by WP 7.4 (ADR-0008 amendment 7): createEngine now draws every frame through the post chain (engine/gfx/post/chain.ts), which makes its targets and builds every pass's pipelines in the warm-up, so a filter or look switch builds nothing; on the default look (look:clean) a frame is plain and draws the scene straight, skipping the chain's passes. The same command, three runs each and the same counts in every run: without the chain, 33 draw calls, 1,823 triangles, 14 textures and 22 pipelines; with it, 33, 1,823, 30 and 66 (16 textures: the scene pass's MRT colour, normal and depth targets, bloom's bright and blur mip targets, the display and FXAA targets; 44 pipelines: the scene's materials for the MRT's targets and every pass of the chain, bloom's included, all in the warm-up); 0 pipelines after the warm-up both ways. These counts are the new budgets. The frame's CPU time was 1.13 to 1.66 ms without the chain (load average 3 to 4) and 0.9 to 1.06 ms with it (load average 6 to 17); the 12 ms budget is kept. Re-recorded by WP 6.7 (ADR-0008 amendment 8): every stage now gives the effects their pools at full size, all warmed up (engine/gfx/stageFx.ts, engine/gfx/fx/effects.ts), so a fight draws with 0 pipelines built after the warm-up. That adds 7 geometries (the sprites' 5 pages, the decals' page and the ribbon mesh) and the pipelines of the effects' 3 materials (sprites, decals, ribbons): 3 without the chain (22 to 25, measured at the lane before it merged WP 7.4) and 9 with it (66 to 75). The same command on the merged tree, three runs with the same counts in each: 33 draw calls, 1,823 triangles, 30 textures, 17 geometries and 75 pipelines, 0 after the warm-up. Draw calls and triangles do not change, since the room has no event or bolt for the effects to draw, nor do textures, since their materials sample none. These counts are the new budgets. The frame's CPU time was 1.06 ms (load average 1); the 12 ms budget is kept. Re-recorded at gate G6's review (ADR-0008 amendment 9): the warm-up compiles for each way a frame draws the scene, the post chain's scene pass and the plain frame, and the level's instanced walls, low walls and pillar have 1,024 slots, so they share their shaders. The same command, three runs with the same counts in each (load average 11 to 24): 33 draw calls, 1,823 triangles, 32 textures (2 more: the 1 x 1 colour and depth of the stand-in target the warm-up compiles the plain frame for), 17 geometries and 24 pipelines, 0 after the warm-up. These counts are the new budgets. The frame's CPU time was 2.1 to 2.2 ms; the 12 ms budget is kept.
